full_judgment: 2. Md Ibrahim (the predecessor-in-interest of the present appellant), as plaintiff, instituted the above mentioned Title Suit No. 190 of 1998 impleading the respondent herein as the sole defendant for declaration that the defendant is 'benamder' of the plaintiff in respect of the properties described in schedule `Ka' and 'Kha' to the plaint and also for declaration of his title in those properties. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the land of schedule 'Ka' originally belonged to Samon Rishi and CS Khatian was prepared in his name. Samon Rishi died leaving two sons, named Hari Mohan and Rai Mohan. Hari Mohan died leaving wife Brahmo Rishi and son Bhagoban Rishi. Bhagoban Rishi died unmarried leaving mother Brohma Rishi as sole heir. That Brahmo Rishi while in possession of her share sold out that to Adu Bepari by kabala dated 14-5-1920. That Rai Mohan, the other son of Samon Rishi died leaving five sons, namely, Rajendra, Kutishar, Naba Rishi, Debendra and Surja Mohan and wife Bidhya Rishi. The said heirs of Rai Mohan transferred their share in favour of Adu Bepari by three registered sale deeds dated 16-7-1920, 18-8-1920 and 12-1-1921. That Adu Bepari thus became the owner of those lands. Adu Bepari leased out 0.0636 acre of land to Nobendra Rishi, Broja Kumar Rishi and Shita Nath Rishi and kept the remaining 0.0774 acre of land in his khas possession. Subsequently Adu Bepari sold out those 0.0774 acre of land to Ganga Charan Saha by kabala dated 12-6-1923. Ganga Charan Saha subsequently sold that land to Bhagaban Chandra Bhowmik by kabala dated 26-1-1927. Bhagaban Chandra Bhowmik subsequently transferred the said land to Kanai Lal Gope by kabala dated 22-2-1939. Kanai Lal Gope while in possession, leased out the same land to the plaintiff by registered deed of lease dated 11-4-1952; said Kanai Lal Gope executed a deed of sale also in respect of the said property in favour of the plaintiff on 12-4-1952 which was registered on the same date. That the plaintiff, out of love and affection, purchased the said land in the name of the defendant who is his cousin and sister-in-law; that plaintiff paid the entire consideration money and purchased the same for his own interest and benefit; that the defendant had no means to pay the consideration. That to maintain the benami character of the suit land the plaintiff had the subsequent record of rights recorded in the name of his 'benamdar'. The plaintiff is in possession of the 'Ka' schedule land. He established a mill under the name and style "Ibrahim Machinery Manufacturing Company" in this 'Ka' scheduled land.
